items.followUp: Define the joule as the SI unit of work.

rubric.why: Identifies the SI unit of potential energy.
rubric.description: Names the joule as the unit.
rubric.how: Award for stating that potential energy is measured in joules (J).

rubric.why: Defines one joule in terms of work done.
rubric.how: Award for stating that one joule is the work done when a force of 1 N moves an object through 1 m in the direction of the force.

modelAnswer: The SI unit of potential energy is the joule (J).
One joule is the work done when a force of 1 N moves an object through 1 m in the direction of the force.

items.followUp: Using a speed-time graph, derive the relation Vf² − Vi² = 2aS.

rubric.why: The area under the speed-time graph gives displacement.
rubric.how: Award for expressing the area of the trapezium under the graph as S = ½(Vi + Vf)t.

rubric.why: Relates acceleration to the change in speed over time.
rubric.how: Award for writing a = (Vf − Vi)/t or rearranging it to find t.

rubric.why: Substitutes for time and combines the graph and acceleration relations.
rubric.description: Eliminates time to form the product.

rubric.why: Uses the difference of two squares to obtain the required result.

modelAnswer: For uniformly accelerated motion, the speed-time graph is a straight line from Vi to Vf over time t.
The displacement S is the area of the trapezium under the graph: S = 1/2(Vi + Vf)t.
Acceleration a = (Vf − Vi)/t, so t = (Vf − Vi)/a.
Substituting for t: 2aS = (Vi + Vf)(Vf − Vi) = Vf² − Vi².

items.followUp: Derive the expression for the kinetic energy of a body of mass m moving with speed v.

rubric.why: Kinetic energy is the energy a body possesses due to its motion.
rubric.how: Award for identifying kinetic energy as energy possessed due to motion.

rubric.why: Relates the kinetic energy gained to the work done on the body.
rubric.description: Expresses kinetic energy as work done.
rubric.how: Award for writing K.E. = W = Fs.

rubric.why: Uses Newton's second law and the motion relation for a body starting from rest.
rubric.how: Award for using F = ma together with v² = 2as, or its rearrangement s = v²/(2a).

rubric.why: Substituting the force and displacement relations gives the kinetic-energy equation.
rubric.how: Award for deriving or stating K.E. = ½mv².

modelAnswer: Kinetic energy is the energy possessed by a body due to its motion.
The kinetic energy gained by a body equals the work done on it: K.E. = W = Fs.
For a body of mass m starting from rest, F = ma and v² = 2as, so s = v²/(2a).
Therefore, K.E. = Fs = ma × v²/(2a) = ½mv².
